name: Visto per motivi di studio (Student visa)

requirement_groups.name: Admitted to a recognised Italian institution

requirements.blocker_text: Requires enrolment confirmation from a recognised Italian university or educational institution for a full-time programme of study.
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission from a recognised Italian institution.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires proof of sufficient financial means for tuition and living costs, plus valid health insurance for the stay.
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements, a scholarship award letter, or a sponsor's financial guarantee.

evidence_required.document: Enrolment confirmation from the Italian institution
Proof of funds or scholarship, and health insurance
Permesso di soggiorno application within 8 days of arrival

outcome.duration_length: tied to course length, renewed via the permesso di soggiorno

sources.title: Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (esteri.it) -- Visto per l'Italia, student visa category

notes: Student permesso di soggiorno holders may work part-time up to 20 hours/week (1,040 hours/year), a real work-rights allowance modeled here as 'restricted' rather than 'none' or 'full' -- distinct from China's confirmed zero-work-rights student status and closer to Poland's more generous allowance, though still capped unlike Poland's uncapped student work rights. Converting a student permesso di soggiorno directly to a work permesso is possible in principle but, as of the 2026 Decreto Flussi cycle, non-seasonal subordinate work conversions from study/training status are explicitly carved out of the click-day quota mechanism (per Circolare interministeriale n. 8047/2025), meaning graduates generally have an easier conversion path than a fresh work-visa applicant competing for click-day quota -- a genuinely favourable structural detail worth flagging.
